summary:
OrbPLUS is an astronaut-facing mission health simulator we built for the “Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions” challenge. It is a frontend-only React app that runs a deterministic simulation in the browser, bringing simulated vitals, mission context, alerts, and crew actions into one interface. Crew members can review a Today view, then open Body, Sleep & Mind, Radiation, Ship & Earth, and EVA sections. In the demo, a simulated solar storm triggers an alert and updates the Radiation view with dose-rate context. The crew member then selects “I am in the shelter” and keeps monitoring until the event eases.

It addresses the challenge by showing how an onboard interface can organize health data so a crew can self-monitor and decide what to do when Earth is far away.

This matters because long missions expose crews to radiation, isolation, altered gravity, and a closed environment. A clear view of changing indicators helps crews act sooner.

OrbPLUS uses simulated data only. It is not clinical software and does not replace medical judgment.
details:
What it does and how it works
OrbPLUS is a mission health simulator for astronauts. It puts simulated vitals, alerts, priorities, trends, and crew actions on one screen. A crew member signs in, reviews the Today view, and opens Body, Sleep & Mind, Radiation, Ship & Earth, or EVA. They can log mood, run an eye check or reaction test, respond to a radiation event, or send a delayed message to Earth. In the demo, a simulated solar storm triggers an alert and updates the Radiation view with dose-rate context. The crew member then selects “I am in the shelter” and keeps monitoring until the storm eases.

Benefits

  • Everything a crew member needs to check sits in one place.
  • Alerts come with context, so the crew can see what changed and what to do.
  • A crew can self-monitor onboard when Earth is far away and messages are delayed.

Intended impact
We want to show how an onboard interface can turn raw signals into awareness, so a crew can notice a change, inspect it, and act sooner. It is a concept for decision support and training, not a clinical tool.

Tools and technology

  • A frontend-only React app (JavaScript) that runs in the browser.
  • A deterministic simulation, so the demo behaves the same every time.
  • GitHub for the code: https://github.com/Zahra8319/Orb-
  • No hardware, wearables, or spacecraft sensors.

What is creative about it
Most health dashboards just display numbers. OrbPLUS is built around a flow of notice, inspect, act, and it ends each scenario with a supported action. The solar-storm walkthrough shows the whole idea in one short demo. We also label simulated data clearly throughout, so nobody mistakes the demo for real telemetry.

What we considered

  • Hazards: we organized the views around NASA’s Human Research Program spaceflight hazards.
  • Honesty: we kept the limits visible. Values are illustrative, nothing is real telemetry, and the app does not diagnose or replace mission procedures or medical judgment.
  • Usability: a crew member under stress needs a clear screen and one next action.
  • Feasibility: a frontend-only, deterministic build lets us demonstrate the concept without sensors or live data.
